StowMind 1.2 adds Agent Cleanup, shared macOS cache diagnostics, and a guided introduction to the app. These notes cover changes since the last published version, 1.0.3.

## Cleanup reliability update

- Recognize current Mole summaries, including “At least” and partially measured results. Keep missing measurements unknown and omit unreported category totals from completed cleanup results.
- Separate Mole's tracked processing amount from reported disk space freed. Files processed or moved to Trash, including installer cleanup and app uninstall results, no longer inflate freed-space statistics.
- Show Mole's summary item count separately from confirmed file-operation records. Preserve confirmed work after partial failures or interruptions, with paged success, failure, and skipped records alongside readable diagnostic output.
- Carry Agent cleanup's known size lower bounds through category previews, selections, confirmations, execution results, history, and statistics; unmeasured items no longer erase known amounts or appear as exact zeroes.
- Rebuild trusted freed-space totals once from verifiable retained history. Preserve history and settings, and retain the previous unverified total for diagnostics; displayed totals may decrease where earlier amounts cannot be verified.
- Place Mole path and scope controls directly above the scan, retry, and cleanup buttons in both page layouts.
- Require fresh, single-use native review tokens for purge and installer cleanup; protect incomplete Agent, Git, and duplicate scans from being treated as empty successful results.
- Add shared total deadlines and cancellation for application inventory, uninstall, and optimization. Confirm process-tree exit before allowing another operation and retain logs and actual partial results after interruption.
- Reduce the initial frontend bundle by separating locale data.

The application version remains 1.2.0 for this explicitly authorized replacement build. Users who already installed the earlier 1.2.0 must download and install the replacement manually; version-only update checks cannot distinguish these builds. The original tag is retained, and the replacement audit identifies its exact new source commit, workflow, and artifact hashes.

## Agent Cleanup

- Preview disposable caches, logs, temporary files, crash reports, and orphaned worktrees for Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, Kiro, Devin, Cursor, Windsurf, Gemini CLI / Antigravity, Continue, GitHub Copilot CLI, Amazon Q Developer, Cline, and Goose.
- Review items by Agent and category with retention rules and explicit selection. Active Agents, configuration, credentials, sessions, and registered worktrees remain protected; incomplete large Crashpad scans cannot authorize cleanup.
- Inspect stale Codex internal Git refs and unreachable Git objects. Git cleanup revalidates repository state and retention rules; object pruning is irreversible, excluded from bulk selection, and requires a separate confirmation.
- Record cleanup results, skipped items, errors, and statistics, then refresh the preview. Ordinary Agent files go to Trash; Git metadata uses Git's own operations.

## Shared system cache diagnostics

- Detect unusually large macOS iconservices caches in Doctor and a separate shared-cache card in Agent Cleanup. Access errors and incomplete measurements remain unknown rather than appearing as zero bytes.
- Keep shared cache measurements independent of Agent scan failures, selections, retention rules, execution, and totals. The cache is shared macOS state and is not attributed to a particular Agent.
- Require separate administrator review and confirmation before scoped Mole cleanup. Recheck the cache afterward and record the outcome and observed size change in system-cache history; this measurement is not claimed as physically reclaimed disk space.

## Everyday use

- Add a guided tour on first use, with controls to skip it or restart it from Settings, and clearer welcome-page links to cleanup features.
- Group repeated watched-folder notifications so saving files does not flood the screen. Make retry actions easier to find after failed scans.
- Improve system monitoring updates and compatibility with older Mole versions, scan diagnostics, and partial-result messages.
- Add Mole whitelist access, external-volume cleanup scope, an option to include empty build-artifact directories, and Mole operation history. Show the installed Mole source and detected capabilities more clearly.
- Load larger frontend features separately to reduce the initial bundle size.

## iPhone Home Screen organization

- Improve complete-page inventory, plan validation, mirroring-window checks, and pause/cancel handling. Failed, paused, or cancelled sessions provide clear retry actions.
- Keep the non-disableable rule that never deletes, uninstalls, hides, removes Apps from the Home Screen, or resets the layout. Assisted moves pause when recognition, window state, or permissions are unsafe.
- Support local Codex CLI and Claude Code alongside the existing AI providers for planning suggestions.

## Permissions and upgrade notes

- Ordinary Agent and shared-cache detection does not request administrator access or remove files. Protected locations may need Full Disk Access; a denied scan remains visible as a permission issue.
- iconservices cleanup is available only on macOS with a compatible Mole runtime. It needs its own administrator review and confirmation, preserves Mole's protection and whitelist rules, and can be refused by those rules. Opening or rescanning Agent Cleanup never authorizes this operation.
- iPhone inventory uses Apple's iPhone Mirroring and needs Screen Recording. Scanning every Home Screen page and assisted moves also need Accessibility; restart StowMind if macOS does not recognize a newly granted permission.
- When upgrading from an older ad-hoc build, remove its old entry in macOS Full Disk Access, add `/Applications/StowMind.app` again, enable access, and restart StowMind. Existing installations already using the same Developer ID identity do not need this migration for every update.
